findings.title: Flagged table widgets render empty data
findings.body: When organization.features includes use-table-widget-visualization, tableResultComponent ignores the widget result and renders TableWidgetVisualization with columns={[]} and tableData whose data, fields, and units are all empty. The real eventView, fields, metadata, and result.data stay on the old StyledSimpleTableChart branch. Enabling the flag therefore blanks every dashboard table widget instead of showing the query results.

findings.title: Replay error context pairs the wrong events and timestamps
findings.body: fetch_error_details zips error_ids with nodestore get_multi(...).values(). get_multi returns a dict keyed by node id and omits missing keys, so values() is not aligned with error_ids: a missing event shifts later payloads onto the wrong ids, and a non-preserving dict order mislabels every error. It also reads data['timestamp'] as a float and gen_request_data compares that to segment event timestamps. Stored events usually keep an ISO datetime (often under datetime) while rrweb segment timestamps are milliseconds, so the comparison either raises TypeError and fails the summarize request, or orders every error at the start of the log.

findings.title: PR comment helpers are not on the workflow that calls them
findings.body: GitHubPRCommentWorkflow and GitlabPRCommentWorkflow call self.get_merged_pr_single_issue_template and self.get_environment_info, but both methods were added to CommitContextIntegration. The template helper then calls PRCommentWorkflow._truncate_title, while _truncate_title is defined on CommitContextIntegration. PR comment workflows do not inherit the integration class, so building a suspect-issue comment raises AttributeError and the GitHub/GitLab comment task fails. Separately, MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE interpolates the title into a markdown link with no escaping, so a title containing ] (typical of exception messages) terminates the link and corrupts the rest of the comment.

findings.title: AI summary treats a still-loading project as missing
findings.body: AiContent now does useProjectFromId({project_id: replayRecord?.project_id}) and, before the pending check, returns an error alert whenever replayRecord.project_id is set and project is falsy. That hook returns undefined both while the project store is loading and when the project is actually missing, so the Replay Summary tab shows "Project not found" and never starts the summarize request until a later render happens to have the project cached. A genuine load is indistinguishable from a missing project.

findings.title: Report age/timestamp validation accepts invalid combinations
findings.body: validate_timestamp treats age as absent when initial_data.get("age") is falsy, so age=0 (a valid Reporting API value meaning the report was just generated) plus a timestamp is accepted. Field validators also never run when the field is omitted, and neither age nor timestamp is required, so a report with neither time field passes. post() then returns 422 for the entire batch on the first invalid item, so one bad report in a browser batch drops metrics for every valid report in that request.

findings.title: Hidden span attributes are only removed while searching
findings.body: HIDDEN_ATTRIBUTES (is_segment, project_id, received) is applied only inside the searchQuery branch. With an empty search the full sorted attribute list is returned, so those fields stay visible in the default span attributes tree. Searching cannot find them either, because the same filter drops them before the name match. If they are meant to be hidden, the exclusion has to run before the search filter, not only when a query is present.

findings.title: Attribute key hook returns undefined after a failed fetch
findings.body: useTraceItemAttributeKeys used to always build a TagCollection object (empty when the request failed or returned nothing). It now returns attributes: isFetching ? previous : data from useQuery. On error, isFetching is false and data is undefined, and the first fetch has no previous value, so attributes is undefined. Callers that spread or iterate attributes without a null check throw, and isLoading is tied to isFetching so background refetches also flip loading even when previous data is on screen.

findings.title: 60s auth-refresh deadline skips identities for a day
findings.body: check_auth_identities now has processing_deadline_duration=60, but it loops a chunk of up to 100 identities and each one can call the IdP via provider.refresh_identity. check_auth already sets last_synced=now before enqueueing this task. If the worker is killed at the deadline, unfinished identities are not refreshed and will not be selected again until the next AUTH_CHECK_INTERVAL (about 22–24 hours), so SSO linked/invalid flags stay stale.
